profile.name: Verina
profile.introduction: With an extensive knowledge of botany, Verina is always solicitous, always smiling, and always wishing for every flower to be blessed with the miracle of life.
profile.review:
Verina is a 5-star Spectro Rectifier Generalist Support who is defined by one of the shortest rotations in the game while having good generalist buffing capabilities, making her fit into a staple character archetype, being able to perform in practically any team composition. Like other characters of her archetype, the buffs she applies are granted to other teammates even upon switching out, and in her case apply to the whole team simultaneously. Verina presents herself as a generalist that’s not only extremely easy to use and understand, but also incredibly quick and effective with buffs that practically have indefinite uptime.

Key Mechanics

Her kit is centered around her Outro skill: she wants to access it as quickly as possible in order to leave the field by providing the surprisingly amazing 15% team-wide all-type DMG amplify for 30s, as well as continuous healing based on her ATK to any character that is or comes on the field for 6s. She has many tools to assist her in that regard.

Her Forte Circuit is the biggest contributor: It holds up to 4 stacks that can be generated by her Intro skill, her Resonance Skill and her fifth Basic Attack. She consumes them with either Mid-Air Attacks or Heavy Attacks (which aren’t used) in order to generate a huge amount of Concerto Energy, and some good bits of healing based on her ATK for your whole party at the same time. 

On top of this, her Inherent Skill provides an additional buff: every time Verina heals, she’s able to provide a 20% team-wide ATK buff for 20 seconds. Alongside the Rejuvenating Glow Echo set, that’s basically the entirety of the extents of Verina’s buffing abilities, and cover her most important kit features.

Rotation Concepts

Verina’s main rotation features are that her Basic Attack 5, Intro and Skill each generate a Forte stack. Verina wants to generate 2 Forte stacks in order to fill her Concerto Gauge up to full. At S2, her Skill is sufficient as it gives 2 Stacks and extra Concerto Energy. That said, at S0, she’ll need to use her Skill and 1 or the other 2 options to get there.

If an Intro is available, even though it’s quite awkward to use as it sends her mid-air for a bit, you can treat it as a lengthy Intro animation until Verina lands back on the ground to preserve decent rotation times. If an Intro is not available, her swap-in attack is Basic 3, so you can skip Basic 1 and 2 simply by switching into her in combat without an Intro. This trick is essential to her optimal rotations.

Her Ultimate is a surge of Concerto that comes with some damage, healing and Coordinated Attacks. Nothing much to say about it other than it’s always important to incorporate in rotations for its Concerto gain.

In other words, Verina’s rotation will consist of her using her Basic 345 or an Intro into her Skill which you can instantly interrupt by her Ultimate, and then two mid-air attacks before an Outro. Without a Concerto weapon available, some extra attacks will be needed, lengthening her rotations a decent amount. Her S2 is the opposite of that, providing huge rotation speed-ups on her No Intro rotations.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Verina’s meta position is probably one of the easiest to understand in the whole game. She’s the free-to-play generalist Support character anyone can use. It’s that easy.

The better a character is at utilizing generalists, the more Verina is capable of replacing the premium Support of a given team. Good examples of teams where Verina fits very well are any 1.x-2.x team other than Lupa, Zani & Cartethyia teams, as well as Sigrika, Hsin Unison and Jingran for the more modern 3.x cast. She additionally features Coordinated Attacks on her Ultimate, so she has an extra synergy with Jinhsi there. Lastly, since her rotation without an Intro is so good (particularly at S2), characters who benefit from Double Intro have that bit of extra team rotation synergy with her. Another niche thing worth keeping in mind is that she can rotate without her Ultimate with an R5 Concerto Weapon, so she can participate in some much shorter team rotations with DPS characters who have an Ultimate cooldown that is very short (e.g Jiyan, Encore).

Otherwise, Verina is completely fine as the best generalist Support choice available for literally any team, ever. That’s her entire meta position: if you don’t have the premium Support for a team, use Verina. She’s indefinitely going to be useful to any account in that position, so she’s always worth grabbing off beginner events that allow you to easily snatch her for free. Her S2 is similarly easily accessible over time, since she’s permanently available.

In conclusion, Verina’s value as a basically-free and generalist Support is easy to understand, she’s easy to play and get a hold of, and while some teams can use her slightly better than others, she can provide some decent and, most importantly, quickly set up buffs in any team whatsoever. That makes Verina a permanently useful character who can serve as the permanent banner replacement to premium Support options when needed.
profile.pros:
• Has one of the shortest rotations in the game by far;

  • Requires very little investment to be effective, can work on a 4* weapon with barely enough Energy Regen to cycle her Ultimate, at which point she provides close to her full value;

  • Very universally strong S2, and decent S4 under specific conditions - rare for permanent banner characters;

  • Can slot in literally any team in the game and at least provide a decent degree of value, if not one of the best/most consistent options on some teams outright;

  • Essentially free - every account can and should get Verina from beginner events/the permanent pool of characters.
profile.cons:
• Her Intro Skill is difficult to maneuver around as it puts her in the air, lengthens her rotations and is best to skip entirely if your characters can benefit from Double Intro - this may require you to adapt team rotations accordingly;

  • Is always outshined by Shorekeeper, who buffs any team a more significant amount. If not her, some other specialized Support will always outmatch Verina. Though this is to be expected of a basically-free character.
profile.endgameStats:
Keep in mind, Verina is a Support who deals very low personal damage, meaning investing in her damage is fully skippable. Energy Regen requirements are by far the most important stat shown.

  • HP: 18000+

  • DEF: 1100+

  • ATK: 1500+

  • CRIT Rate: 60%+

  • CRIT DMG: 210%+

  • Energy Regen: 220%-230%

    • Less Energy Regen (around 200%) can be required if Verina’s skill hits the enemy, however it’s better to interrupt it via her Ultimate to save time and hence this Energy requirement should be fulfilled as a priority.

  • Spectro DMG Bonus: 0-30%
profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Verina is a very straight-forward character who wants to build up 2 Forte Stacks consumed via Mid-Air Attacks to generate a full Concerto gauge as quickly as possible. Concerto weapons help with this, and her S2 does too. Based on what’s available for her to generate Concerto quicker, as that is her only priority, below are the rotations that can help you do so as quickly as possible.

Echo Timing

Use Fallacy of No Return at the end of her rotation right before Outro, for maximum buff uptime on your secondary and your main damage dealer.

No Intro R1+ Rotation

Used on every rotation after the first, if Verina’s teammates have no significant benefit from Introing twice. However, if they do, you may prioritize that and choose to perform the No Intro rotation every time instead.

  • Switch-in from any other character in combat 

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic 5 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill (Instantly interrupt animation via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Jump

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 1

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 2 

  • Outro

S2+ No Intro Rotation

It’s strongly recommended, if possible, to skip Verina’s Intro at S2+ because she gets to perform the much faster rotation below on every rotation. It’s always worth it to do this, unless Verina is strictly required to Intro in, like in an Augusta team for example.

  • Switch-in from any other character in combat 

  • Skill (Instantly interrupt animation via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Jump

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 1

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 2 

  • Outro

No Intro R0 Rotation

Used on every rotation after the first, if a Concerto weapon is not available and Verina’s teammates have no significant benefit from Introing twice. However, if they do, you may prioritize that and choose to perform the No Intro rotation every time instead.

  • Switch-in from any other character in combat 

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic 5 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill (Instantly interrupt animation via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Jump

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 1

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 2 

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack 3

  • Outro

Intro R1+ Rotation

The rotation below looks the same at S2+, though it isn’t recommended to do if you have the option of doing a No Intro rotation (you have that option on almost any team other than with Augusta, for example):

  • Intro

  • Skill (Instantly interrupt via Ultimate) 

  • Ultimate 

  • Jump 

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 1

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 2

  • Outro

R0 Intro Rotation

Used if a Concerto weapon is not available.

  • Intro

  • Skill (Instantly interrupt via Ultimate) 

  • Ultimate 

  • Basic 1 (Cancel animation endlag via Jump)

  • Jump 

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 1

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms 2

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack 3

  • Outro

Additional Tips & Tricks

At R5 Variation, Verina can also rotate without an Intro or an Ultimate available. This can help in teams with very short Ultimate cooldowns to do very quick team rotations: some Jiyan or Encore teams can make use of this via their 16 second-long Ultimate cooldown, for example. To do this, simply do the No Intro rotation with an extra Mid-Air Attack at the end.

Additionally, performing Perfect Dodges or Parries can help with rotating quicker at S0R0, as they can give quick surges of Concerto needed to get an Outro as quickly as S0R1.

skills.name: Cultivation
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Verina performs up to 5 consecutive attacks with vines, dealing Spectro DMG.

Heavy Attack

Verina consumes Stamina to charge forward, dealing Spectro DMG.

Mid-air Attack

Verina consumes Stamina to perform up to 3 consecutive attacks in mid-air, dealing Spectro DMG.

Mid-air Heavy Attack

Hold Basic Attack to consume Stamina and perform mid-air Plunging Attack, dealing Spectro DMG..

Dodge Counter

Use Basic Attack after a successful Dodge, to attack the target, dealing Spectro DMG.

skills.name: Botany Experiment
skills.description: Verina converges an energy field in front to grow foliage, dealing Spectro DMG within the range.

skills.name: Arboreal Flourish
skills.description:
Verina nourishes nearby foliage at rapid speed, dealing Spectro DMG while restoring HP to all team members nearby. A Photosynthesis Mark is applied to the target on hit.

Photosynthesis Mark

Whenever a team member nearby performs an attack on targets with a Photosynthesis Mark, Verina performs a Coordinated Attack, dealing Spectro DMG while restoring HP to the party members dealing damage, triggered once per second.

skills.name: Starflower Blooms
skills.description:
Heavy Attack: Starflower Blooms

When casting Heavy Attack, if Verina carries "Photosynthesis Energy", Verina consumes 1 stack of "Photosynthesis Energy" to recover Concerto Energy and restore HP for all party members nearby; Heavy Attack: Starflower Blooms deals Spectro DMG, considered as Heavy Attack damage.

Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms

When casting Mid-air Attack, if Verina carries "Photosynthesis Energy", Verina consumes 1 stack of "Photosynthesis Energy" to recover Concerto Energy and restore HP for all party members nearby; Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms deals Spectro DMG, considered as Basic Attack damage. Verina can cast Mid-air Attack: Starflower Blooms by using Basic Attack after casting Heavy Attack: Starflower Blooms.

Photosynthesis Energy

Verina can hold up to 4 "Photosynthesis Energy". Verina obtains 1 stack of "Photosynthesis Energy" for every Basic Attack V on hit; Verina obtains 1 stack of "Photosynthesis Energy" for every Resonance Skill Botany Experiment on hit; Verina obtains 1 stack of "Photosynthesis Energy" for every Intro Skill Verdant Growth on hit.

skills.description: Verina protects a party member from fatal damage and grants a shield with strength equal to 120% of Verina's ATK, lasting for 10s. This can be triggered once every 10 minutes.

skills.description: When Verina casts Heavy Attack Starflower Blooms, Mid-air Attack Starflower Blooms, Resonance Liberation Arboreal Flourish or Outro Skill Blossom, ATK for all party members is increased by 20% for 20s.

skills.name: Blossom
skills.description: Verina recovers HP to The next character (or other characters on a nearby team that activates an Outro Skill) equal to 19% of her ATK per second for 6s. All Characters on nearby teams gain 15% all-Type DMG Deepen for 30s.

dupes.dupe1: Outro Skill Blossom grants the next character a continuous Healing effect, recovering HP equal to 20% of Verina's ATK every 5 seconds for 30s.
dupes.dupe2: Resonance Skill Botany Experiment additionally grants 1 [Photosynthetic Energy] and 10 Concerto Energy.
dupes.dupe3: Healing of Resonance Liberation's Photosynthesis Mark is increased by 12%.
dupes.dupe4: Heavy Attack Starflower Blooms, Mid-Air Attack Starflower Blooms, Resonance Liberation Arboreal Flourish and Outro Skill Blossom increases the Spectro DMG Bonus of all team members by 15% for 24s.
dupes.dupe5: When Verina heals a team member with HP less than 50%, her Healing is increased by 20%.
dupes.dupe6: Heavy Attack Starflower Blooms and Mid-Air Attack Starflower Blooms deal 20% more damage. They will trigger Coordinated Attack 1 time and heal all characters nearby. The DMG of this Coordinated Attack and the Healing are equal to those of the Resonance Liberation's Photosynthesis Mark.

profile.synergyNote: Verina can be used literally anywhere and perform amazingly as she’s the second best Support in the game, very slightly behind Shorekeeper. She’s even the best in some Jinhsi teams that use secondaries that don’t have Coordinated Attacks, and some quickswap teams that prefer her lower field time!
profile.teamsNote: Verina is very flexible and can be used in any team in the Support slot.

weapons.Comment: Without a doubt the best option on Verina, that enables her to cut down one attack in her rotation and as such shave even more time off her already super short rotation, effectively boosting her team's DPS even more. The Energy Regen is also a really nice substat for Verina (and her best one at that.)
The best option for Verina that doesn't require any gacha. Provides a big amount of Energy Regen and a small ATK% boost when casting Skill, acquired for free via crafting.

More healing-focused option for Verina which is also given for free via an Exploration quest in Rinascita. Provides the same amount of Energy Regen as the above options, but has the added pro of increasing Healing Bonus by 16% for 15s when casting Ultimate. Better than Rectifier#25 if the player desires more healing on the team, but it is not a necessity.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Simple summon Echo that can be cast any time (ideally right before the wielder's Outro), granting 10% ATK to the team for 20s (sufficient for 2 other teammates' rotation times if cast right before Outro) as well as 10% Energy Regen to the wielder to help with Energy requirements.
